entries.title: Parity Multisig — initWallet hijack
entries.summary: Public initWallet on a deployed multisig allowed any caller to overwrite ownership and drain the wallet.
entries.root_cause: Initializer was not access-controlled and could be re-invoked after deployment.
entries.impact: Approximately 153,037 ETH drained from a single wallet.
entries.attacker_path: Call initWallet to overwrite owners, then withdraw wallet balance.
entries.invariant_broken: Wallet owners can be set only once, by the deployer.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed initWallet was bound to the constructor; deployment pattern made it post-callable.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker EOA ETH balance after attack > pre-attack balance + ~150,000 ether.
entries.victim_loss_check: Multisig wallet ETH balance after attack equals zero.

entries.title: Parity Wallet Library — suicide
entries.summary: Anyone could initialize and then self-destruct the shared library that all Parity multisigs delegated to, freezing every dependent wallet.
entries.root_cause: Library contract had unprotected initialization and a privileged kill function reachable through delegatecall semantics.
entries.exploit_primitive: unprotected initialization plus self-destruct on shared library
entries.attacker_path: Initialize the shared library to take ownership, then call its kill function.
entries.invariant_broken: A shared library cannot be self-destructed by an unrelated caller.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed the library was permanently anchored by its consumers; nothing prevented direct ownership.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Library is selfdestructed; downstream wallet calls revert. (No direct attacker profit.)
entries.victim_loss_check: Library code at the well-known address is empty post-suicide; dependent wallets cannot delegatecall.

entries.title: BeautyChain (BEC) — batchTransfer overflow
entries.summary: Integer overflow in batchTransfer minted an arbitrary number of BEC tokens to attacker addresses, collapsing the token's market.
entries.root_cause: Unchecked multiplication of (count * value) in pre-0.8 Solidity allowed wraparound when both factors were large.
entries.impact: BEC token economically destroyed; trading halted on major exchanges.
entries.attacker_path: Call batchTransfer with crafted (count, value) pair that overflows count*value.
entries.invariant_broken: totalSupply equals sum of holder balances; transfers conserve supply.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed solidity arithmetic could not overflow at realistic input sizes.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker BEC balance after attack approximates the overflowed supply.
entries.victim_loss_check: Token totalSupply no longer matches sum of legitimate holder balances.

entries.title: SpankChain — payment channel reentrancy
entries.summary: Reentrancy in the payment-channel close path drained the SpankChain hub contract.
entries.root_cause: External call to a user-controlled token before state update in the channel close handler.
entries.impact: Approximately 165 ETH plus BOOTY balances drained.
entries.exploit_primitive: external token call before state update on channel close
entries.attacker_path: Open channel, trigger close path, reenter via ERC-20 token call before balance state is updated.
entries.invariant_broken: A channel close transfers exactly its remaining balance, once.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker ETH and BOOTY balances after attack > pre-attack + reentered withdrawals.
entries.victim_loss_check: SpankChain hub contract balance < pre-attack balance by the drained amount.

entries.title: Uniswap V1 — imBTC reentrancy
entries.summary: ERC-777 transfer hook in imBTC enabled cross-function reentrancy against Uniswap V1's ETH→token swap path.
entries.root_cause: Uniswap V1 swap path performed external token transfer before updating internal reserves, and imBTC's ERC-777 _callTokensReceived gave the attacker control mid-execution.
entries.impact: Approximately 1,278 ETH and 24.5 imBTC drained from Uniswap pools.
entries.exploit_primitive: ERC-777 transfer hook re-entering Uniswap V1 swap path
entries.attacker_path: Initiate Uniswap V1 ETH->imBTC swap; reenter inside ERC-777 hook before reserves update.
entries.invariant_broken: Pool reserves are consistent with executed swaps when the next read occurs.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed ERC-20 transfers do not yield control to the recipient.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker ETH balance after attack > pre-attack balance plus drained pool ETH minus loan fees.
entries.victim_loss_check: Uniswap V1 pool ETH and imBTC reserves < pre-attack reserves by the drained amounts.

entries.title: Balancer — deflationary token rounding
entries.summary: Repeated swaps with a deflationary token (STA) skewed pool weights and let the attacker drain other tokens.
entries.root_cause: Pool accounting assumed transferred amount equaled requested amount; fee-on-transfer tokens broke that invariant.
entries.impact: Approximately $500k in WETH, WBTC, LINK, and SNX drained.
entries.attacker_path: Repeatedly swap STA against the pool so transfer fee skews weights, then withdraw other tokens.
entries.invariant_broken: Pool weights and balances reflect the tokens actually held.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed transferred amount equals requested amount for all listed tokens.
entries.victim_loss_check: Balancer pool token balances < pre-attack balances for the drained tokens.

entries.title: Opyn — duplicate ETH option exercise
entries.summary: Opyn's exercise function summed msg.value across an array of options, letting one ETH payment exercise multiple option lots.
entries.root_cause: Loop over options used the single msg.value as collateral for each iteration instead of dividing it.
entries.impact: Approximately $370k of collateral drained from ETH put vaults.
entries.exploit_primitive: msg.value reused across array iterations in exercise
entries.attacker_path: Call exercise with multiple option lots so loop reuses single msg.value as collateral for each.
entries.invariant_broken: Each exercised option lot is collateralized by its own ETH payment.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed each option in the array independently bore its own collateral payment.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker collateral output > sum of legitimate per-option payments.
entries.victim_loss_check: Opyn vault collateral balance < pre-attack balance by the over-exercised amount.

entries.title: bZx — iToken duplicate transfer
entries.summary: iToken transfer logic let a user transfer to themselves and double their balance.
entries.root_cause: _internalTransferFrom updated source then destination from cached values, but with self-transfer the second write overwrote the first.
entries.impact: Approximately 219,200 LINK plus other assets drained.
entries.attacker_path: Call iToken transfer to self so destination write overwrites source decrement, doubling balance.
entries.invariant_broken: Internal token transfer preserves the sum of source and destination balances.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed source and destination of an internal transfer are different addresses.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker post-redemption asset balance > pre-attack balance.
entries.victim_loss_check: iToken vault asset balance < pre-attack balance by the duplicated redemption.

entries.title: Harvest Finance — fUSDT/fUSDC oracle manipulation
entries.summary: Flash-loan-funded swap on Curve Y-pool moved the spot price Harvest used to mint fTokens, letting the attacker mint cheap and redeem high.
entries.root_cause: Harvest derived share price from the same Curve pool the attacker could move with a single flash loan.
entries.impact: Approximately $33.8M drained from fUSDT and fUSDC vaults.
entries.attacker_path: Flash loan, swap to imbalance Curve Y-pool, deposit into Harvest at distorted price, withdraw, reverse swap.
entries.invariant_broken: fToken share price reflects fair value of underlying, independent of intra-tx pool moves.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed Curve spot price was a usable proxy for fair price within one transaction.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker stablecoin balance after attack > flash-loan principal plus fees.
entries.victim_loss_check: fUSDT/fUSDC vault underlying balance < pre-attack balance.

entries.title: Cheese Bank — Uniswap LP price oracle manipulation
entries.summary: Attacker manipulated a Uniswap V2 spot price used by Cheese Bank as collateral oracle and borrowed against an inflated LP valuation.
entries.root_cause: Cheese Bank priced LP collateral from instantaneous Uniswap reserves rather than a TWAP, letting a flash-loan-funded swap distort the value within one transaction.
entries.impact: Approximately $3.3M in DAI, USDC, and USDT drained.
entries.exploit_primitive: flash-loan-funded Uniswap V2 spot LP price manipulation
entries.attacker_path: Flash loan, swap to move Uniswap reserves Cheese reads, borrow against inflated LP collateral, reverse.
entries.invariant_broken: LP collateral value reflects fair LP value, independent of intra-tx Uniswap moves.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed Uniswap V2 reserves at the moment of read reflect fair LP value.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker stablecoin balance after attack > flash-loan principal plus fees.
entries.victim_loss_check: Cheese Bank stablecoin reserves < pre-attack reserves.

entries.title: Warp Finance — LP token oracle manipulation
entries.summary: Flash-loan-funded swap moved the Uniswap pool reserves Warp used to value LP collateral, enabling oversized stablecoin borrows.
entries.root_cause: LP collateral valuation derived from current pool reserves without manipulation-resistant pricing.
entries.impact: Approximately $7.7M in DAI and USDC drained.
entries.exploit_primitive: flash-loan-funded Uniswap reserve manipulation for LP collateral
entries.attacker_path: Flash loan, swap to move Uniswap reserves Warp reads, borrow stablecoins, reverse.
entries.invariant_broken: LP collateral value reflects fair LP value, independent of intra-tx pool moves.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed Uniswap reserves at the moment of read reflect fair LP value.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker stablecoin balance after attack > flash-loan principal plus fees.
entries.victim_loss_check: Warp Finance stablecoin reserves < pre-attack reserves.

entries.title: Saddle Finance — early swap rounding
entries.summary: Early-deposit rounding allowed a small but reproducible value extraction against the Saddle stablecoin pool.
entries.root_cause: Stable-swap math rounded fee accounting in the depositor's favor under specific imbalanced-pool conditions.
entries.impact: Limited; primarily a soft-loss / fee-skim issue rather than a full drain.
entries.notes: Original PoC author flagged the file as incomplete. Listed for historical record; assertions should be tightened before promoting status.
entries.attacker_path: Deposit small imbalanced amount, exit at a slightly favorable share price.
entries.invariant_broken: Round-trip deposit and withdraw on a stable-swap pool returns approximately the original value, minus fees.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed stable-swap rounding could not be amplified into a repeatable extraction.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker net asset value after deposit/withdraw cycle > inputs minus fees.
entries.victim_loss_check: Pool reserves drift in attacker's favor over the cycle (small, repeatable).

entries.title: Yearn v1 DAI vault — Curve 3pool oracle manipulation
entries.summary: Attacker imbalanced the Curve 3pool around the yDAI vault's deposit and withdrawal calls, extracting value via the share-price difference.
entries.root_cause: Vault accounting depended on the spot virtual price of a Curve pool the attacker could push and pull with flash loans within one transaction.
entries.impact: Approximately $11M of DAI/USDC/USDT extracted from the yDAI vault.
entries.attacker_path: Flash loan, imbalance Curve 3pool around yDAI deposit and withdraw, capture share-price delta.
entries.invariant_broken: yDAI share price reflects fair value of underlying, independent of intra-tx Curve moves.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed Curve virtual-price was usable as oracle within one transaction.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker stablecoin balance after attack > flash-loan principal plus fees.
entries.victim_loss_check: yDAI vault underlying balance < pre-attack balance.

entries.title: DODO — CrowdPooling init reentrancy
entries.summary: DODO crowdpools could be re-initialized after the first init, letting the attacker repoint the pool at malicious tokens and drain liquidity.
entries.root_cause: init function lacked a guard against re-entry / re-initialization, and flash-loaned reserves left the legitimate state replaceable mid-call.
entries.exploit_primitive: re-initialization of crowdpool with attacker tokens
entries.attacker_path: Flash-loan reserves, call init again with attacker-controlled tokens, drain liquidity.
entries.invariant_broken: init runs exactly once and binds the pool's tokens for its lifetime.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed init was guarded against re-entry once liquidity was present.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker token balance after drain > attacker tokens supplied.
entries.victim_loss_check: Crowdpool reserves < pre-attack reserves; reserve token now attacker-controlled.

entries.title: Indexed Finance — DEFI5/CC10 reweight manipulation
entries.summary: During an index reweighting, the attacker swung weights with a flash loan such that a small input minted a disproportionate amount of index tokens, then redeemed the underlying basket.
entries.root_cause: Reweighting math allowed an attacker-supplied imbalance to dominate the new weights, breaking the invariant that the pool was worth its underlying basket during the transition.
entries.impact: Approximately $16M drained from DEFI5 and CC10 indices.
entries.attacker_path: Flash-loan supply, dominate reweight inputs, mint outsized index tokens, redeem underlying basket.
entries.invariant_broken: Index token mint price equals the fair basket value during reweighting.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed reweight inputs were bounded by realistic counterparty capital.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker basket-asset balance after redeem > pre-attack basket-asset balance.
entries.victim_loss_check: DEFI5 / CC10 underlying balances < pre-attack balances.

entries.title: Dexible — preApproved selfSwap drain
entries.summary: Dexible's selfSwap path forwarded calls to attacker-controlled targets, letting the attacker move tokens that users had pre-approved to the router.
entries.root_cause: Router did not validate the swap target, so any address could be invoked with the user's pre-approval still active.
entries.impact: Approximately $2M drained across multiple users with active token approvals.
entries.exploit_primitive: router with pre-approved tokens forwarded to attacker target
entries.attacker_path: Call selfSwap with attacker-controlled target so router uses pre-approved user tokens.
entries.invariant_broken: Router only forwards user-approved tokens to user-intended destinations.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed selfSwap target was always a vetted DEX adapter.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker token balance after call > pre-attack balance, sourced from victim approvals.
entries.victim_loss_check: Victim wallet token balance < pre-attack balance for previously approved tokens.

entries.title: Moonwell — Chainlink oracle staleness on Base
entries.summary: Moonwell's price feed returned a stale value for a market on Base, letting an attacker borrow against inflated collateral.
entries.root_cause: Oracle wrapper did not enforce freshness against the underlying Chainlink answer's updatedAt timestamp under the conditions present at the attack block.
entries.impact: Approximately $1M extracted from a single market.
entries.exploit_primitive: stale Chainlink answer accepted at borrow time
entries.attacker_path: Borrow against a market while its Chainlink feed is returning a stale (favorable) price.
entries.invariant_broken: Borrow accounting reads only fresh oracle prices.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed Chainlink answers were always fresh enough for instantaneous use.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker borrowed-asset balance > borrow input value at fair price.
entries.victim_loss_check: Moonwell market collateral / reserves < pre-attack balance.

entries.title: yETH — pool invariant manipulation
entries.summary: A multi-phase sequence of add_liquidity, remove_liquidity, rate updates, and an OETH rebase manipulated the yETH pool's vb_prod_sum invariant, ending with a full pool drain.
entries.root_cause: yETH's stable-swap-style invariant could be steered through a specific sequence of liquidity moves and rate updates, breaking the relationship between LP supply and underlying assets.
entries.impact: Approximately $9M drained from the yETH pool.
entries.exploit_primitive: multi-step liquidity / rate / rebase sequence steering pool invariant
entries.attacker_path: Sequence add_liquidity, remove_liquidity, rate updates, OETH rebase to steer vb_prod_sum, then drain.
entries.invariant_broken: yETH pool invariant is preserved across any sequence of valid liquidity moves and rate updates.
entries.protocol_assumption_failure: Assumed every reachable sequence of liquidity moves and rate updates left the pool's value-conservation invariant intact.
entries.attacker_profit_check: Attacker pool-asset balance after sequence > pre-attack balance.
